name: LFO vs envelope: cyclic vs note-triggered motion
goal: Use LFOs for repeating/cyclic motion (tremolo, vibrato, wobble, WT/PWM drift; audio-rate into AM/FM) and envelopes (ADSR) for note-triggered shapes—amp envelope for dynamics, filter envelope with ±amount for pluck/wah—then route either modulator to WT position or pulse width for evolving pads.

source.title: Sound Design Theory: LFO & Envelope explained!

prerequisites: Synth or Web Audio graph with at least one LFO, one ADSR, amp, and filter cutoff destination

inputs.name: destination
inputs.description: amp, pitch, cutoff, PWM, wavetable position, FX param

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI (Serum/Vital/Ableton/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable parameter relationships over vendor-specific preset or bank names.
LFOs and envelopes are control modules—they make no sound alone; movement is the design goal.

steps.action: Treat LFO as a very slow oscillator (usually below hearing): set shape (sine/tri/square/saw/custom) and rate, then assign to a destination so the parameter follows the oscillation.

Classic LFO recipes: → amp = tremolo; → pitch = vibrato; → low-pass cutoff = wobble; → waveform/PWM/WT position = evolving source timbre. Tempo-sync for rhythmic motion or keep slow free-rate for subtle drift.
steps.expect: Audible cyclic change on chosen param

steps.action: Raise LFO rate into audio range: amp mod → AM sidebands; pitch mod → FM-like spectra; very fast FX-param mod (e.g. phaser) can become a distortion/timbre effect.
If available, try LFO one-shot mode—shape plays once, behaving like an envelope.

Amp envelope ADSR: Attack = fade-in time; Decay = time to sustain; Sustain = held level (if sustain = max, decay has no effect); Release = fade-out after key-up. Percussive: attack+sustain low, length from decay (+ some release). Pad/violin-like: longer attack+release, sustain full.

Filter envelope: assign to cutoff with ±amount/depth. Positive amount opens from a low cutoff (plucky bass with short A, some D, no S, short R). Negative amount with high cutoff can wah downward; longer attack + positive amount opens wah; raise sustain to keep open while held.
Ensure amp envelope lets enough signal through to hear filter motion. Also try envelopes on PWM or wavetable position so the source evolves per note.

verification: LFO motion repeats without new notes; envelope retriggers per note
Amp + filter envelopes cooperate (filter decay audible under amp)
